Conclusions
Vitamin D plays a key role in the regulation and maintenance of innate immunity. A poor vitamin D status is related to non-
communicable chronic diseases, namely obesity, metabolic syndrome, T2DM, cancer, RA, COPD, and IBD. Also, a low vitamin
D status is associated with an increased incidence of acute respiratory illnesses of both bacterial and viral origin. Likewise, low
25(OH)D levels are associated with a worse prognosis of patients with acute illness. Well-designed randomized intervention clinical
trials addressed to evaluate the efﬁcacy of administration of vitamin D and its metabolites for the treatment of both chronic and
acute diseases are needed.
